children.text: catvāraḥ pākayajñā huto 'hutaḥ prahutaḥ prāśita iti ||
children.translated_text: There are four pākayajñas: the offered, the unoffered, the abundantly offered, and the eaten.

children.text: pañcasu bahiḥśālāyāṃ vivāhe cūḍākaraṇa upanayane keśānte sīmantonnayana iti ||
children.translated_text: In five cases, outside the hall: at marriage, at the tonsure, at initiation, at the first shaving of the beard, and at the parting of a pregnant woman's hair.
When the place has been smeared, swept up, and sprinkled, he should bring forward the fire.
Some say that at a marriage it should be produced by churning.

children.text: udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇyāhe kumāryai pāṇiṃ gṛhṇīyāt ||
children.translated_text: During the sun's northward course, in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious day, he should take the hand of the maiden.
She should be one who is endowed with auspicious marks.
One whose limbs are fitting in relation to her self.
The ends of her hair should be even.
And if she has two curls on her neck, turning clockwise,
he should know that she will bear six heroic sons.
When he is about to take a wife, he addresses those going as suitors with the verse beginning 'anṛkṣarā'.
At the approach, they take flowers, fruits, barley, and also a water-pot.
Having said three times, 'Here I am,'

children.text: udite prāṅmukhā gṛhyāḥ pratyaṅmukhā āvahamānā gotranāmānyanukīrtayantaḥ kanyāṃ varayanti ||
children.translated_text: when the sun has risen, the members of the bridegroom's party, facing east, and those bringing the bride, facing west, reciting their gotra names, ask for the girl.

children.text: ubhayato rucite pūrṇapātrīm abhimṛśanti puṣpākṣataphalayavahiraṇyamiśrām anādhṛṣṭam asyānādhṛṣṭyaṃ devānām ojo 'nabhiśastyabhiśastipā anabhiśastenyam añjasā satyam upa geṣaṃ suvite mā dhā iti ||
children.translated_text: When both sides have approved, they touch a full vessel mixed with flowers, unbroken grains, fruits, barley, and gold, saying, 'Unassailed is she; may she be unassailable, the vigor of the gods, protecting from accusation and from what is accused; with unaccused straight truth I shall approach. Set me in good fortune.'

children.text: ā naḥ prajām iti kanyāyā ācārya utthāya mūrdhani karoti prajāṃ tvayi dadhāmi paśūṃstvayi dadhāmi tejo brahmavarcasaṃ tvayi dadhāmīti ||
children.translated_text: With 'Bring us offspring,' the ācārya rises and places it on the girl's head, saying, 'I place offspring in you; I place cattle in you; I place splendor and brahmic radiance in you.'
When the promise has been made, he offers oblations.
Having smeared a square altar-space with cow dung,
for the ancestral rite he makes the southern line, facing east, in the two eastern intermediate directions.
For the divine rite, the northern one.
Some prescribe only an eastward one.
Having drawn a line in the middle, ending toward the north,

children.text: tasyai dakṣiṇata upariṣṭād ūrdhvām ekāṃ madhya ekām uttarata ekāṃ ||
children.translated_text: he draws one vertical line above it on the south side, one in the middle, and one on the north side.
Having sprinkled these,

children.text: agniṃ praṇayāmi manasā śivenāyam astu saṃgamano vasūnām
children.translated_text: he brings the fire forward with, 'I bring the fire with a kindly mind; may this be the meeting-place of the Vasus.

children.text: mā no hiṃsīḥ sthaviraṃ mā kumāraṃ śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade
children.translated_text: Do not harm our elder, nor the child; be gracious to our two-footed and gracious to our four-footed.'
Thus he brings the fire forward.
Or silently.

children.text: pradakṣiṇam agneḥ samantāt pāṇinā sodakena triḥ pramārṣṭi tat samūhanam ity ācakṣate ||
children.translated_text: With his hand containing water he wipes around the fire clockwise three times; that they call the sweeping-together.
Once counterclockwise in the ancestral rite.
Then comes the strewing around.

children.text: prāgagraiḥ kuśaiḥ paristṛṇāti trivṛt pañcavṛd vā ||
children.translated_text: He strews kuśa grasses with their tips toward the east, in threefold or fivefold arrangement.

children.text: purastāt prathamam atha paścād atha paścāt ||
children.translated_text: First in front, then behind, then again behind.
He covers the roots with the tips.
And all the turns begin from the south and end toward the north.

children.text: dakṣiṇato brahmāṇaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the brahman-priest to the south, saying, 'bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svar,'
and having adorned him with kindly thoughts,

children.text: uttarataḥ praṇītāḥ praṇīya ko vaḥ praṇayatīti ||
children.translated_text: he brings the praṇītā waters to the north, saying, 'Who brings you forward?'
Taking kuśa grasses with the left hand, he removes them with the right.
Having bent down the right knee.
The left knee in the ancestral rite.
There is not always a strewing around for ājya-offerings.
<s>Māṇḍūkeya</s> says that there is also strewing around for the regular oblations.

children.text: kuśataruṇe aviṣame avicchinnāgre anantargarbhe prādeśena māpayitvā kuśena chinatti pavitre stha iti ||
children.translated_text: Having measured, by the span, two young kuśa blades that are even, with unbroken tips and without inner hollowness, he cuts them with a kuśa blade, saying, 'You are the purifiers.'
There may be two or three.
Holding them with their tips toward the east, he sprinkles them with 'You are of Viṣṇu.'
With the two young kuśa blades he sprinkles around the fire clockwise three times.
Taking the ghee-vessel with 'You are the milk of the great ones,'
he sets it on the fire with 'For refreshment you,'
and removes it northward with 'For strength you.'

children.text: udagagre pavitre dhārayann aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ copakaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ cobhayataḥ pratigṛhyordhvāgre prahve kṛtvājye pratyasyati savituṣṭvā prasava utpunāmyacchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhir iti ||
children.translated_text: Holding the purifiers with their tips toward the north, grasping them on both sides with the thumbs and little fingers, making them point upward and bend forward, he casts them into the ghee, saying, 'By the impulse of Savitṛ I purify you with an unbroken purifier, with the rays of Vasu Sūrya.'
The preparation of the ghee applies everywhere.
He should not offer with unprepared ghee.
And water in the ladle, with 'of Savitṛ' or the like.
These are the praṇītā waters and also the sprinkling waters.
The ladle is the vessel.
The taking is determined by the purpose.

children.text: savyena kuśān ādāya dakṣiṇena mūle sruvaṃ viṣṇor hasto 'sīti ||
children.translated_text: Taking kuśa grasses with the left hand, with the right he takes the ladle at its root, saying, 'You are Viṣṇu's hand.'
With the ladle he offers the ghee-oblations.

children.text: uttarapaścārdhād agner ārabhyāvicchinnaṃ dakṣiṇato juhoti tvam agne pramatir iti ||
children.translated_text: Beginning from the northwestern half of the fire, he offers continuously toward the south with 'You, Agni, are forethought.'

children.text: dakṣiṇapaścārdhād agner ārabhyāvicchinnam uttarato juhoti yasyeme himavanta iti ||
children.translated_text: Beginning from the southwestern half of the fire, he offers continuously toward the north with 'Whose are these Himalayas.'
The northern portion of ghee belongs to Agni, the southern to Soma.
The other oblations are in the middle.

children.text: 'gnir janitā sa me 'mūṃ jāyāṃ dadātu svāhā somo janimān sa māmuyā janimantaṃ karotu svāhā pūṣā jñātimān sa māmuṣyai pitrā mātrā bhrātṛbhir jñātimantaṃ karotu svāheti ||
children.translated_text: 'Agni is the begetter; may he give me this wife, svāhā. Soma is possessed of birth; may he make me possessed of birth through this woman, svāhā. Pūṣan is possessed of kin; may he make me possessed of kin through her father, mother, brothers, and relatives, svāhā.'
In ājya-offerings the two regular portions of ghee and the sviṣṭakṛt are not constant.
<s>Māṇḍūkeya</s> says that they are so also in the regular oblations.
This is the place of insertion after the great vyāhṛtis, the general expiation, and the prājāpatya oblation.

children.text: ājye haviṣi savye pāṇau ye kuśās tān dakṣiṇenāgre saṃgṛhya mūle savyena teṣām agraṃ sruve samanakti madhyam ājyasthālyāṃ mūlaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: When the oblation is ghee, he takes with the right hand the tips of those kuśa grasses that are in the left hand; with the left he grasps their roots, and he anoints their tips in the ladle, their middle in the ghee-vessel, and their roots too.

children.text: atha cet sthālīpākeṣu srucy agraṃ madhyaṃ sruve mūlam ājyasthālyām ||
children.translated_text: But in cooked offerings, the tip is in the offering-spoon, the middle in the ladle, and the root in the ghee-vessel.
Having thrown them in afterward, he says, 'You are the garment of Agni.'
Having laid on three fuel-sticks,
The sprinkling around is as stated.

children.text: anāmnātamantrāsv ādiṣṭadevatāsv amuṣyai svāhāmuṣyai svāheti juhuyāt svāhākāreṇa śuddhena ||
children.translated_text: When the mantras are not specified but the deities are indicated, he should offer saying, "To this one, svāhā; to this one, svāhā," with the pure utterance of <s>svāhā</s>.
The procedure for an oblation in response to a request has been explained.
It is the model for prosperity rites.
And for all offerings of clarified butter.
For animals of the branch.
And for sacrifices involving the cooking of <s>caru</s>.

children.text: ta ete 'prayājā ananuyājā anilā anigadā asāmidhenīkāś ca sarve pākayajñā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus all these pākayajñas are without fore-offerings, without after-offerings, without the <s>iḍā</s>, without formal proclamation, and without kindling-verses.
On this too there are verses.
It is offered by the agnihotra-oblation; it is unoffered by the bali rite.
It is well-offered by the ancestral rite; it is offered when it has been eaten by a Brahmin.
One should always offer the oblation without raising the knees, with the knees set apart.

children.text: na hi bāhyahutaṃ devāḥ pratigṛhṇanti karhicit ||
children.translated_text: For the gods never accept an offering made outside.

children.text: raudraṃ tu rākṣasaṃ pitryam āsuraṃ cābhicārikam
children.translated_text: But in rites to Rudra, to rākṣasas, to the Fathers, to asuras, and in hostile sorcery,

children.text: uktvā mantraṃ spṛśed apa ālabhyātmānam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: after uttering the mantra, he should touch water and then touch himself.

children.text: athaitāṃ rātrīṃ śvas tṛtīyāṃ vā kanyāṃ vakṣyantīti ||
children.translated_text: Now, on this night, or on the third night from tomorrow, they will announce the maiden.
On that night, when the night-time has passed,

children.text: sarvauṣadhiphalottamaiḥ surabhimiśraiḥ saśiraskāṃ kanyām āplāvya raktam ahataṃ vā vāsaḥ paridhāya ||
children.translated_text: having bathed the maiden, including her head, with the best fruits of all herbs mixed with fragrant substances, and having put on a red or new garment,

children.text: paścād agneḥ kanyām upaveśyānvārabdhāyāṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhir hutvājyāhutīr juhoti
children.translated_text: he seats the maiden west of the fire, and, while she is held from behind, having offered butter-offerings with the great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, he offers
to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Mitra</s>, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Indrāṇī</s>,

children.text: gandharvāya bhagāya pūṣṇe tvaṣṭre bṛhaspataye rājñe pratyānīkāyeti ||
children.translated_text: to the <s>Gandharva</s>, to <s>Bhaga</s>, to <s>Pūṣan</s>, to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, to the king, and to <s>Pratyānīka</s>.

children.text: catasro 'ṣṭau vāvidhavāḥ śākapiṇḍībhiḥ surayānnena ca tarpayitvā catur ānartanaṃ kuryuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Four or eight women whose husbands are living, having satisfied her with balls of greens, liquor, and food, should make her dance four times.
These same deities are used for a male.
And <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>.
After this comes the feeding of Brahmins.

children.text: snātaṃ kṛtamaṅgalaṃ varam avidhavāḥ subhagā yuvatyaḥ kumāryai veśma prapādayanti ||
children.translated_text: Young women whose husbands are living, fortunate and auspiciously adorned, lead the bathed and ceremonially prepared bridegroom to the maiden's house.
He should not oppose them, except in cases involving forbidden food or sin.

children.text: tābhir anujñāto 'thāsyai vāsaḥ prayacchati raibhy āsīd iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, with their permission, he gives her a garment, saying, "She was <s>Raibhī</s>."
Saying, "Perception is the cushion," he takes up the box of collyrium.
"May all the gods anoint together" is the formula for anointing.

children.text: yatheyaṃ śacīṃ vāvātāṃ suputrāṃ ca yathāditim
children.translated_text: "As this one has been loved like <s>Śacī</s>, and as she is blessed with good sons like <s>Aditi</s>,

children.text: avidhavāṃ cāpālām evaṃ tvām iha rakṣatād imaṃ iti
children.translated_text: as a woman with a living husband and free from misfortune, so may he protect you here, this man,"
he places a threefold <s>śalalī</s> in her right hand.
Saying, "Form after form," he places a mirror in her left hand.

children.text: raktakṛṣṇam āvikaṃ kṣaumaṃ vā trimaṇiṃ pratisaraṃ
children.translated_text: Her relatives bind on her a three-jeweled protective band, red and black, made of wool or linen,
saying, "dark-blue and red."
Saying, "The honey-sweet herbs," he fastens pieces of madhūka wood.

children.text: vivāhe gām arhayitvā gṛheṣu gāṃ te mādhuparkikyau ||
children.translated_text: At the wedding, after honoring a cow, in the houses the two cows for the honey-mixture belong to you.

children.text: paścād agneḥ kanyām upaveśyānvārabdhāyāṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhis tisro juhoti ||
children.translated_text: Having seated the maiden west of the fire, and while she is held from behind, he offers three oblations with the great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>.
With all of them together, he should understand a fourth oblation in this injunction.

children.text: evam anādeśe sarveṣu bhūtikarmasu purastāccopariṣṭāc caitābhir eva juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when there is no special prescription, in all prosperity rites he should offer both before and after with these same formulas.
